blocks.text: Why tracking lumper fees kills your margin

A freight broker lumper fee is often a small, variable expense that is easy to overlook until it accumulates. When you handle these fees manually, you invite three specific types of risk into your workflow. First, you risk simple data entry errors. Typing a fee as 150 instead of 15.00 can cause massive reconciliation headaches later. Second, you risk losing the receipt itself. Without a clear digital trail, you cannot bill the shipper, which means you pay the carrier out of your own pocket. Third, you face the time penalty. If you spend 10 minutes chasing a receipt for a 50 fee, you have already lost money on that load.
Common causes of expense tracking errors

items: Reliance on email chains to track lumper receipts instead of a centralized platform.
Delayed entry of expenses into the TMS, leading to forgotten costs during final billing.
Lack of standardized naming conventions for digital files, making it impossible to search for specific receipts.
Manual reconciliation of carrier invoices against load confirmations, which is prone to human error.

blocks.text: Fixes you can use right now

You do not need expensive software to start fixing your expense tracking. Start by creating a dedicated folder structure in your cloud storage. Use a consistent naming format like YYYY-MM-DD-LoadNumber-LumperReceipt. This makes searching for documents in Finder much faster. Next, set a rule to process all incoming carrier emails at the same time each day. Do not leave them in your inbox. If you use Gmail, create a label specifically for receipts and use the search bar to filter by subject line. When you receive a receipt, drag it directly into your TMS or your designated folder immediately.

faq.question: How do I handle lumper fees if my TMS does not support them?
faq.answer: If your TMS lacks a specific field, use the notes section or a custom field if available. Always attach the digital receipt to the load record immediately.

faq.question: Can I use my Mac for all freight brokerage tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. Most modern TMS platforms are cloud-based and run perfectly in Chrome or Safari. Avoid legacy software that requires Windows unless you use virtualization tools.
